title: PSE&G Prepared for Strong Winds and Heavy Rain on Thanksgiving
body_markdown:
1. Newsroom


# PSE&G Prepared for Strong Winds and Heavy Rain on Thanksgiving


## Utility takes steps to protect customers and communities while encouraging everyone to prepare and stay safe; Follow us on social media for more details


(NEWARK, N.J. – Nov. 24, 2026) – PSE&G is closely monitoring a strong coastal storm expected to bring damaging wind gusts, heavy rain and the potential for coastal flooding to parts of New Jersey on Thanksgiving Day. The company has activated its storm response plan, mobilized additional crews and strategically positioned personnel and equipment across its service territory for a fast, coordinated response.


PSE&G has additional line personnel, tree crews and support staff ready to respond if the storm damages electric equipment or brings trees and branches onto power lines. Operations teams will monitor weather conditions and system performance around the clock, allowing the company to adjust resources and response plans as conditions evolve and deploy crews where customers need them most.


These preparations reflect PSE&G's ongoing efforts to strengthen the electric system, improve reliability and resilience, and keep customer affordability in focus.


“Our crews are ready to respond wherever they're needed,” said John Latka, senior vice president, PSEG operations. “We know how important reliable electric service is, especially as families and friends gather for Thanksgiving. We're taking steps now to prepare for the storm, with the safety of our customers, employees and communities at the forefront. If outages occur, we'll be there to restore service as quickly and safely as possible.”


Throughout the storm, PSE&G will remain in close communication with county and local emergency management officials and other public safety partners to help coordinate response efforts as needed.


PSE&G's customer-facing teams, including representatives in the call center and across the company's communications channels, will remain active to provide updates to customers as conditions change.


PSE&G encourages customers to prepare before the storm arrives:


- Charge cell phones and other essential electronic devices.
- Keep flashlights and fresh batteries readily available. Avoid using candles whenever possible.
- Secure or bring inside outdoor furniture, umbrellas, grills and other loose objects that could become airborne in strong winds.
- If you rely on electrically powered medical equipment, have a backup plan in place.
- Never touch or approach[downed power lines](https://nj.pseg.com/safetyandreliability/electricsafety/downedpowerlines) . Always assume they are energized and dangerous. Stay at least 30 feet away and report them immediately.
- [Use portable generators only outdoors](https://nj.pseg.com/safetyandreliability/stormsafety/generatorsafety) and well away from windows, doors and vents to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.


Customers who rely on electricity to operate life-sustaining medical equipment should notify PSE&G in advance by visiting[pseg.com/life](https://nj.pseg.com/safetyandreliability/electricsafety/lifesustainingequipment) or calling1-800-436-7734 , and should have a backup plan in the event of an outage.


Customers can report outages and monitor restoration progress by:


- Using the PSE&G mobile app
- Visiting[pseg.com/outagecenter](https://nj.pseg.com/outagecenter)
- Texting “OUT” to 4PSEG (47734)
- Calling1-800-436-PSEG (7734)


Customers are encouraged to sign up for outage alerts to receive updates by text, email or phone and follow PSE&G on social media:[@PSEG](https://www.facebook.com/PSEG/) on Facebook and[Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/pseg/?hl=en) and[@PSEGdelivers](https://x.com/PSEGdelivers?lang=en) on X.


PSE&G reminds customers that restoration work begins only after conditions are safe for crews to perform their work. During widespread outages, crews first assess damage across the electric system to determine restoration priorities before beginning repairs. Restoration efforts focus first on repairing damage that returns power to the greatest number of customers, while also restoring service to critical facilities such as hospitals, emergency response agencies and other essential infrastructure.


PSE&G will continue providing updates through its Outage Center, mobile app and social media channels as conditions warrant. If the severity of the storm or its impacts change significantly, the company will provide additional information as it becomes available.


For additional storm safety information, outage updates and restoration information, visit[pseg.com/outagecenter](https://nj.pseg.com/outagecenter) .


Emergency preparedness isn't only for utility crews and first responders. The PSEG Foundation and Sesame Workshop have developed research-based extreme weather preparedness resources designed to help young children and families build resilience and navigate weather-related emergencies. The resources include educational videos, family guides and printable activities that support learning and preparedness in engaging, age-appropriate ways.


For more information and to access these resources, visit[Sesame Workshop's PSEG Foundation partnership page](https://sesameworkshop.org/about-us/partners/pseg-foundation/) .
